# Workshopr Design System

> The shared visual language for every Workshopr app — tokens, components, voice, and rules. This file orients AI agents and points to the machine-readable sources. Read START-HERE.md for the full hierarchy.

Source-of-truth order (higher wins), from START-HERE.md, which also ranks the written spec and is the full version: `/DESIGN.md` + `/motion.md` (intent) → `platform-tokens.css` + `helpers.php` (implementation) → `components.generated.json` (the agent contract, generated from them) → `workshopr-design-system.json` (hand-maintained rules and curated option lists) → the `.php` demos.

## Read first

- [START-HERE.md](START-HERE.md): the entry point — source-of-truth hierarchy + on-ramps for designer / developer / AI.
- [/DESIGN.md](../DESIGN.md): canonical brand, voice, visual system, UX principles, forms.
- [/motion.md](../motion.md): motion stack, easings, durations, animation patterns.

## Machine-readable

- [components.generated.json](components.generated.json): read this first. Every `ws_*` helper with its signature, the only option values each option takes, a canonical `example`, `whenToUse` / `whenNotToUse`, `insteadOf`, `a11y` (prose, or one `Concern: behavior` line per rule where the demo has a table) and `antiPattern`; every token with its value, tier and, where documented (every brand and semantic token), its `purpose`; each component's `tokens` and each token's `usedBy` (from the `components.css` rules); the legacy lookalikes to avoid; and the screen recipes. Generated by `generate-catalog.php`, never hand-edited.
- [knowledge-graph/knowledge-graph.json](knowledge-graph/knowledge-graph.json): the same facts as edges, with the rules added: component draws-with token, token references token, component calls component, component instead-use component or recipe, recipe uses component, legacy pattern replaced-by, rule mentions. Before changing a token or a helper, run `npm run ds:graph -- <name> --impact` for everything it reaches, including the pages, scripts and stylesheets it reads live.
- [workshopr-design-system.json](workshopr-design-system.json): the hand-maintained `rules` block (`componentFirst`, `tokenFirst`, `phaseColors`), phases, apps and the curated option lists the catalog merges.
- [tokens.dtcg.json](tokens.dtcg.json): all tokens in W3C DTCG format with `$type` and `var()` aliases — for Style Dictionary, Figma, Tokens Studio, and AI tooling.
- [platform-tokens.css](platform-tokens.css): the source-of-truth CSS variables.

## Rules (non-negotiable)

- Component-first: use a `ws_*` helper from `/includes/components/helpers.php` before writing raw HTML. In JavaScript, call its twin in `/js/ws.js` (the catalog entry's `js` field, such as `ws.button(text, options)`) rather than writing `ws-*` markup.
- Token-first: use CSS variables; never hardcode a hex or px value when a token exists.
- Layout-first: space and arrange components with `ws_stack_start`, `ws_cluster_start`, `ws_grid_start` and `ws_container_start` (each closed by its `_end`), not a page-local flex or grid rule.
- Inside `/app/`, a view's layout is the page grid: `.app-page` holds a six-column `.app-page__main` (928) and the two-column rail (296), on eight columns of `--app-grid-col` with `--app-grid-gutter`. `design-system/apps/app-shell-layouts.php` has the details.
- Phase colors: all phases use the unified Learn Red family. Read DESIGN.md for sanctioned exceptions; do not restore retired phase colors.
- Type: Fraunces (H1–H3) + Inter (body, H4+). Grays: warm Tailwind Stone, never cool gray. No pure black text, no pure white page background.

## Validate before finishing

- `design-system-enforcer` MCP: `suggest_component`, `list_components`, `list_tokens`, `check_snippet`, `validate_file`, `audit_page`, `fix_file` and `native_apps`. Run it on any UI you produce. `check_snippet` takes `code` and `language` (`css`, `php`, `js` or `swift`); in PHP it reports a raw `<button>`, `<select>`, `<textarea>` or non-hidden `<input>` as `raw-control`. No check here tests accessibility, so read the rendered page's accessibility tree too. START-HERE.md step 5 has what each check covers.
- `php design-system/tools/check-drift.php` — JSON ↔ tokens/helpers drift guard.
- `php design-system/tools/generate-catalog.php --check` and `php design-system/tools/generate-tokens-dtcg.php --check` — confirm the generated files are current.

## Find, preview, verify

- `npm run ds:find -- "describe the UI need" --json`: ranked helpers, usage, options, examples and demo paths from the generated catalog.
- [playground.php](components/playground.php): editable, database-free component fixtures and matching PHP.
- `npm run check:ds -- <changed PHP/CSS files>`: local gates and isolated browser/visual tests. Also exercise the actual application page.
- See CLAUDE.md §11 for baseline review and the required handoff to Bill.

## Native apps

- [native.md](docs/native.md): the three SwiftUI apps (Back Pocket, Field Guide, Workshopr Planner for Mac). Their values live only in each app's theme files and mirror `platform-tokens.css`; a view never holds a colour literal.
- The `native` block of [workshopr-design-system.json](workshopr-design-system.json) binds each app to its paths, project, scheme, theme files and sanctioned scopes. The MCP's `native_apps` prints it, and `list_tokens` with `platform: "swift"` and an `app` shows each token as a Swift colour beside the constants that mirror it.
- `npm run lint:ds:native`: the Swift rules over every app, failing on any finding the baseline does not hold. `validate_file` runs the same rules on one file.

## The design agent

- The `design-agent` plugin runs `/design-loop <target>`: a director builds, an independent `design-agent:design-critic` scores each rendered pass, and the loop stops at an exit bar that includes 0 new enforcer violations on the files it touched. It asks the enforcer MCP before building and checks with it after.
- Its source is `agents/design-agent/plugin/`; `/agents/` is gitignored, so its files exist only in a local checkout, never in git or CI.
